title: Stream-slate adaptor SDK ergonomics — PRD sketch
content:
Context / summary:
This is a lightweight PRD sketch for a Stream Slate Adaptor: an SDK and hosted-api pattern to support incremental streaming with fine-grained action-tiling, typed tool-handshakes, and compact structured envelopes targeted at low-latency clients (mobile, edge) and high-throughput servers. The goal is to give teams an ergonomic client surface that reduces integration complexity while exposing performance levers (prefetch budgets, tile sizes, jitter budgets).

Problem statement (why):
- Developers building composable UX layers (in-app assistants, code editors, search assistants) need predictable partial results for progressive rendering and tool invocation. Existing streaming surfaces either force full JSON reassembly on client or leave ad-hoc heuristics for partial tool calls.
- Tool calling and structured output are brittle under intermittent networks and small token budgets; clients then implement messy fallbacks.
- SDK ergonomics today require heavy client-side machinery to stitch sequences, replay partial outputs, and reconcile tool confirmations. This increases integration time and error surface.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce average integration time for an assistant-like app by 40% (developer time to implement streaming + tool calls).
- Provide a compact framing that reduces client-side reassembly CPU by 25% for common micro-session patterns.
- Guarantee that partial tool-call frames can be safely retried/idempotent with clear semantics (no double-actuation).
- Expose latency- and cost-control knobs so teams can trade fidelity vs. token-unit cost.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full replacement for long-lived session persistence or offline-first replication.
- Not addressing model-level quality evaluation in this doc (handled by Optimize/evals).

High-level approach / primitives:
- Slate: a server-side transient object representing a micro-session fragment (0..N tokens, one or more micro-actions). Slates are atomic from client view: a slate may contain zero or more incremental text updates and zero or more tool-call events (invocation request / confirmation / result).
- Tile: each slate is sliced into ordered tiles (small frames) to improve incremental delivery and allow partial rendering. Tiles are id-tagged and carry a slot-range to reassemble without holding whole slate in memory.
- Typed Envelope: structured payload schema (compact JSON-LD-ish envelope) that includes minimal typing metadata (type, version, idempotency-key, sequence-index, partial=true/false). Clients can parse minimally and render incrementally.
- Micro-transaction semantics: tool calls inside a slate are 2-phase: request frame (optimistic) and finalization frame. Optimistic frames include a safe shadow (intent-id) enabling rewind or no-op on duplicate deliveries. Finalization frames contain authoritative result and cost tokens used.

Protocol sketch (wire semantics):
- Initial request: client opens a streaming call as usual but includes header: X-Stream-Slate: enable=true; slate-policy={tiling, jitter-budget-ms, max-tiles}.
- Server response: multiplexed stream of frames. Each frame is one tile in a slate envelope. Frames are labeled with: slate-id, tile-index, tile-count, envelope-version, type (delta|tool-req|tool-result|checkpoint).
- Retrying: if client sees missing tile(s) in a slate after jitter-budget, it requests a resync endpoint with slate-id+range. Server may return a compact diff or full tile depending on retention policy.

Structured output and tool handshake model:
- Tool-call lifecycle: tool-req tile (includes intent-id, tool-schema-ref, args-summary), tool-ack tile (server acknowledges queued/forwarded), tool-result tile (result payload + result-metadata).
- Idempotency: intent-id + server-assigned activation-token ensure tool routers can deduplicate. Activation-token included in finalization frame to be used for reconciliation/logging.
- Partial result semantics: a tool-result can stream incremental patches of the result; each patch is an ordered tile. If the client misses patches, it can request a patch-range reconciliation.

SDK ergonomics (client-facing surface):
- Surface API (JS/TS pseudo):
  const stream = client.stream({model, slate: {policy: 'tiling', maxTiles: 8}})
  stream.on('tile', (tile) => {
    if (tile.type === 'delta') renderIncremental(tile.text)
    if (tile.type === 'tool-req') updateUIForToolInvocation(tile.intentId, tile.toolSummary)
    if (tile.type === 'tool-result') applyToolPatch(tile.intentId, tile.patch)
  })
  stream.on('checkpoint', (meta) => commitLocalState(meta.slateId))
- Helper primitives in SDK:
  - SlateReconciler: lightweight in-memory manager that stores incomplete slates keyed by slate-id and exposes events when a slate reaches terminal state.
  - IntentManager: client-side mapping intent-id -> UI token; handles safe replays and de-duplication on reconnect.
  - PatchApplier: applies ordered patches to structured result objects without full rehydrate.
- Default ergonomics: provide minimal glue for web and React Native (tiny package ~4KB gzip) and a richer Node helper for server-side BFFs that need to stitch tool-calls across users.

Backwards compatibility / migration path:
- If X-Stream-Slate header absent, server falls back to conventional stream behavior (existing incremental tokens).
- Feature-gated: server advertises support in OPTIONS or capability endpoint. SDK auto-detects.

Observability and debugging primitives:
- Events to emit: slate-created, slate-completed, tool-intent-fired, tool-activation, tile-missing-resync, tile-latency. Each event includes slate-id and tile indexes.
- Sampling: default 1% of slate events sampled to traces; can be overridden per-customer.
- Cost telemetry: token-accounting attached to finalization frames, exposed via Console per-route and per-slate aggregation.

Operational considerations:
- Retention window: short (seconds to minutes) by default for tile replay; policy configurable per-customer (Dedicated/Private may extend).
- Memory vs latency tradeoff: bigger tile sizes reduce per-frame overhead but increase latency; surface recommends an adaptive policy that increases tile-size after warmup.
- Safety: tool-req frames must be validated by the routing layer; execution is only performed upon server-side finalization unless explicit execution flag is set (risky).

Security and compliance notes:
- Slate envelopes must not carry PII in unencrypted headers; recommend payload-level encryption for sensitive fields (KMS).
- Activation-tokens treated as audit keys and should be rotatable.

Developer experience and docs plan:
- Quickstart: "Add X-Stream-Slate header" sample for JS, Python, and mobile SDK.
- Cookbook: patterns for progressive search result pages, in-editor code actions, mobile low-bandwidth assistants.
- Migration guide: fallbacks and common pitfalls (replay storms, double-actuation).

Open questions / risks:
- How to expose a single consistent semantics for tools that have external side-effects (email send, billing) vs read-only tools? (Need product-policy: optimistic vs confirmed execution).
- Retention cost vs value: how long to keep tiles for resync in hosted offering vs Dedicated?
- Complexities around cross-slate tool references (tool A result referenced by tool B in later slate). Do we permit cross-slate referents or force canonicalization?

Next steps / proposals for immediate sprints:
- Spike (1 week): implement server-side tile encoder and a minimal replay endpoint; create a lab client that renders incremental tiles and exercises tool handshake.
- UX work (1.5 weeks): SDK minimal API + React example + small sample-app showing progressive tool invocation.
- Instrumentation (1 week): add slate events + Console view prototype for slate-level traces and token accounting.
- Security review (1 week): threat model for optimistic tool delivery and activation tokens.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and focused on developer ergonomics first. We should prioritize a safe-by-default mode where tool execution requires explicit finalization confirmation from server.
- Looking for feedback on: tile sizing defaults, idempotency-key semantics, retention defaults for hosted vs dedicated, and any canonical schema patterns we should standardize across products.

Embeds / examples (short):
- Example tile envelope (compact):
  {"v":"1","sid":"s-8f3","i":2,"t":"tool-req","id":"intent-42","payload":"{tool:search, argsSummary:'query: foo'}"}
- Example usage note: clients should always surface a transient UI token for tool intent and treat final tool-result as authoritative.

-- Sofia
Draft status: alpha/prd-sketch.
